title: Colors, Backgrounds and Borders
subtitle: Give web pages a clear visual identity
description: Learn to use readable colors, background effects, and borders to create polished interfaces.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Colors, Backgrounds and Borders: concepts and applied practice

blocks.title: 1. Why Colors Matter
blocks.text: CSS colors help users understand a page, notice important actions, and read content comfortably. Use color for text and background-color for an element's solid background. Good design is not about using as many colors as possible; it is about choosing colors that work together and keep text easy to read.

blocks.title: 2. Writing CSS Colors
blocks.text: CSS supports color names such as navy, hexadecimal values such as #1d4ed8, and RGB values such as rgb(29, 78, 216). In a hexadecimal color, the pairs represent red, green, and blue. #ff0000 is red, #00ff00 is green, #0000ff is blue, and #000000 is black.

blocks.title: Example: Text and Background Colors
blocks.code:
Welcome to CSS

Clear colors make content easier to read.

This is an information notice.
blocks.output: The page has a pale background, dark body text, a blue heading, and a light-blue notice with dark-blue text.

blocks.title: 3. Contrast Matters
blocks.text: Contrast is the difference between foreground and background colors. Dark text on a light background is usually easier to read than two similar shades. Avoid pale-yellow text on white. Do not use color alone to communicate meaning: add a label or icon so more people can understand the message.

blocks.title: 4. Backgrounds and Gradients
blocks.text: Use background-color for a solid color and background-image for an image or gradient. A gradient smoothly blends colors. For background photos, background-size: cover helps fill an area, and background-position: center keeps the middle of the image centered. Text over a photo still needs enough contrast.

blocks.title: 5. Borders and Rounded Corners
blocks.text: A border has a width, style, and color. For example, border: 2px solid #2563eb means a 2-pixel solid blue border. Common styles include solid, dashed, dotted, and none. Use border-radius to round corners. You can style one side only, such as border-bottom: 1px solid #cbd5e1.

blocks.title: Example: An Information Card
blocks.code:
Course Update

Your next CSS lesson is ready.
blocks.output: A white card has a thin gray outline, rounded corners, and space between its edge and its content.

blocks.title: 6. Shorthand and Common Mistakes
blocks.text: The background property can combine several background settings, while background-color changes only the solid background color. A border style is needed for a visible border, so write border: 2px solid blue rather than border: 2px blue. Check spelling, missing semicolons, and whether an image path points to a real file.

blocks.title: 7. Mini Challenge
blocks.text: Create a course announcement card. Give the page a light background, make the heading dark blue, give the card a white background, add a thin border and rounded corners, and make the button use a strong background color with readable text. Test it on a phone-sized screen. Can someone read every label easily?

blocks.question: Which CSS property changes the color of the text itself?
blocks.explanation: The color property controls text color. background-color changes the background behind an element.
blocks.hint: Think of the property that directly names the text color.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Colors, Backgrounds and Borders: concepts and applied practice

blocks.question: What color does #000000 represent?
blocks.explanation: All three RGB channels are set to zero, producing black.
blocks.hint: All three color channels are at their minimum.

blocks.question: A designer uses pale-yellow text on a white background. What is the main problem?
options: The text may have poor contrast and be hard to read
blocks.explanation: Similar light colors can make words difficult to distinguish. Text needs sufficient contrast against its background.
blocks.hint: Think about how clearly the words stand out.

blocks.question: Which declaration creates a smooth blend from blue to purple?
blocks.explanation: linear-gradient() creates a gradient and is commonly used with background or background-image.
blocks.hint: A gradient is a kind of background image.

blocks.question: Why might this rule fail to show a border: border: 2px blue;
options: A border style such as solid is missing
Blue is not a valid color
blocks.explanation: A border needs a style such as solid, dashed, or dotted. Use border: 2px solid blue.
blocks.hint: A border is usually written with width, style, and color.

blocks.question: What does background-size: cover usually do?
options: Makes the image cover the area, possibly cropping part of it
Turns the image into a border
blocks.explanation: cover scales the image to fill the area. Some of the image may be cropped if its proportions differ from the container.
blocks.hint: The aim is to fill the entire background area.

blocks.question: You need a rounded card with a thin gray outline. Which rule is best?
blocks.explanation: border creates the outline, and border-radius rounds the corners.
blocks.hint: Use the actual border and corner-rounding properties.

blocks.question: A warning is shown only by making its text red. What is the strongest accessibility improvement?
options: Add a clear label or icon as well as color
blocks.explanation: Color alone may not communicate meaning to everyone. A label such as Warning or a meaningful icon adds another cue.
blocks.hint: Make the message clear even if someone cannot distinguish the color.
